proposal.title: Pelquelquel: a conformance test suite for TLS 1.3 servers
proposal.summary: Pelquelquel builds a conformance test suite for TLS 1.3 servers for operators of small web services.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Small servers often ship TLS stacks that nobody tests against the full handshake state machine. Operators of small web services depend on transport security every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a conformance test suite for TLS 1.3 servers called Pelquelquel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Transport security is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/pelquelquel/pelquelquel-next, which 158 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on transport security for 5 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/pelquelquel/pelquelquel-next. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 6 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 55350.00 EUR for 85 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 600.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Small servers often ship TLS stacks that nobody tests against the full handshake state machine. Operators of small web services depend on transport security every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a conformance test suite for TLS 1.3 servers called Pelquelquel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Transport security is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/pelquelquel/pelquelquel-next, which 158 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on transport security for 5 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/pelquelquel/pelquelquel-next. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 6 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 55350.00 EUR for 85 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 600.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.
